question: What is the maximum age in days for a newborn to be considered as having neonatal sepsis?
explanation: Neonatal sepsis is an infection that happens within the first twenty-eight days of life, which is the standard neonatal period. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T1#BMP220_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why is it so important for midwives to spot neonatal sepsis early, especially in settings with limited resources?

options.A: Newborns in Nigeria are naturally immune to all bacteria
options.B: Lab tests can completely replace a physical checkup
options.C: Advanced intensive care units are available in every rural clinic
options.D: A baby can get very sick quickly before lab results come back

explanation: Because sepsis moves fast and testing can take time, midwives must rely on physical signs to start care and save lives promptly. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T1#BMP220_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which bacteria is most commonly linked to early-onset neonatal sepsis worldwide?
explanation: Group B Streptococcus and Escherichia coli are the leading global causes of infections that show up in the first few days of life. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T1#BMP220_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the term for an infection passed from the mother's birth canal to the baby during delivery?
explanation: Vertical transmission happens when germs pass from mother to baby either across the placenta during pregnancy or through the birth canal during delivery. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T1#BMP220_U2_T1_h2)

question: Within how many hours of birth does early-onset neonatal sepsis usually show up?
explanation: Early-onset neonatal sepsis typically appears within the first 72 hours of life because the baby catches the infection from the mother. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T1#BMP220_U2_T1_h3)

question: A ten-day-old baby in the nursery develops an infection while in the hospital. How is this classified?
explanation: Infections that show up after 72 hours of life, especially in hospital settings, are grouped as late-onset sepsis. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T1#BMP220_U2_T1_h3)

question: Which body temperature change is most often seen in newborns with severe systemic sepsis?

options.B: Low body temperature or unstable temperature

explanation: Newborns often react to severe bacterial infections by running a low body temperature instead of the high fevers seen in older children. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T1#BMP220_U2_T1_h4)

question: A mother says her two-day-old baby boy is refusing feeds and sleeping much more than usual. What should the midwife suspect?
explanation: Poor feeding and unusual sleepiness in the first days of life are key warning signs of early-onset neonatal sepsis. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T1#BMP220_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is considered the gold standard test to confirm a diagnosis of neonatal sepsis?
explanation: Growing and identifying the germ through a blood culture remains the most reliable way to confirm neonatal sepsis. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T1#BMP220_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why is it important to collect blood for cultures BEFORE giving the first dose of antibiotics?

options.A: To keep the antibiotics from killing the bacteria in the sample and hiding the infection
options.B: To give the baby time to rest before injections
options.C: To prevent antibiotics from staining the lab glass slides
options.D: To ensure the lab technician is paid in advance

explanation: Starting antibiotics before drawing blood can temporarily clear the bacteria from the sample, leading to a false-negative result and a missed diagnosis. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T1#BMP220_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which combination of medicines is usually given first when treating suspected neonatal sepsis?
explanation: Ampicillin paired with an aminoglycoside like gentamicin provides broad coverage against the most common early-onset newborn infections. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T1#BMP220_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is the main goal of antibiotic stewardship in a newborn ward?

options.A: To make sure every newborn gets at least three different antibiotics
options.B: To reduce the cost of buying syringes
options.C: To remove the need for blood cultures entirely
options.D: To prevent drug-resistant bacteria by using targeted drug choices

explanation: Antibiotic stewardship avoids unnecessary broad-spectrum drug use, helping to prevent the rise of resistant superbugs in vulnerable babies. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T1#BMP220_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why is keeping a baby warm using an incubator or warmer so important when they have sepsis?

options.A: It helps the baby absorb oral vitamins faster
options.B: It removes the need to check the baby's heart rate
options.C: It cures the bacterial infection without needing drugs
options.D: It prevents cold stress that can worsen the baby's acid-base balance

explanation: Cold stress forces the baby's body to use up more oxygen and energy, which deepens acidosis and makes a septic newborn much sicker. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T1#BMP220_U2_T1_h7)

question: A newborn with severe sepsis has a swollen tummy and trouble breathing. What is the safest immediate feeding plan?

options.A: Give cow milk in a feeding bottle right away
options.B: Stop oral feeds and provide nutrition through a drip
options.C: Give traditional herbal drops to clear the bowel
options.D: Force full volume feeds to keep weight up

explanation: A swollen tummy and breathing trouble mean high risk for aspiration or gut injury, so stopping oral feeds and using intravenous support is safest. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T1#BMP220_U2_T1_h7)

question: Which umbilical cord care practice is currently recommended to prevent stump infections?

options.A: Keeping the cord clean and dry
options.B: Binding the cord tightly with a dirty cloth
options.C: Applying fresh palm oil every day
options.D: Dabbing it with saliva and herbal mixtures

explanation: Health guidelines recommend dry cord care and avoiding the application of unhygienic substances to the umbilical stump. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T1#BMP220_U2_T1_h8)

question: How do clean practices during labor directly help lower the rates of newborn infections?

options.A: By stopping germs from traveling up into the amniotic fluid
options.B: By removing the need for Vitamin K injections
options.C: By shortening the second stage of labor
options.D: By helping the baby produce more red blood cells

explanation: Keeping things clean during labor stops vaginal and environmental bacteria from reaching the fetus before birth, reducing early sepsis. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T1#BMP220_U2_T1_h8)
